policy.rationale: Gloss phrasing differences between sources of different eras are expected nuance (info readings), not findings. Disagreement is reserved for objective-equality facts. Nothing is auto-resolved; readings are verbatim. Caveat: 'agree' for glosses is computed on the first ';'/':' segment, so a multi-sense gloss truncated to its first sense can agree with a single-sense reading — consult the verbatim readings.

verse_text.note: single source — cross-translation comparison arrives with additional verse_text sources

verse_text.note: single source — cross-translation comparison arrives with additional verse_text sources

verse_text.note: single source — cross-translation comparison arrives with additional verse_text sources

verse_text.note: single source — cross-translation comparison arrives with additional verse_text sources

readings.value: And to rule over the day and over the night, and to divide the light from the darkness: and God saw that it was good.

verse_text.note: single source — cross-translation comparison arrives with additional verse_text sources

readings.value: And the evening and the morning were the fourth day.

verse_text.note: single source — cross-translation comparison arrives with additional verse_text sources

verse_text.note: single source — cross-translation comparison arrives with additional verse_text sources

readings.value: And God created great whales, and every living creature that moveth, which the waters brought forth abundantly, after their kind, and every winged fowl after his kind: and God saw that it was good.

readings.value: And God blessed them, saying, Be fruitful, and multiply, and fill the waters in the seas, and let fowl multiply in the earth.

verse_text.note: single source — cross-translation comparison arrives with additional verse_text sources

readings.value: And God said, Let us make man in our image, after our likeness: and let them have dominion over the fish of the sea, and over the fowl of the air, and over the cattle, and over all the earth, and over every creeping thing that creepeth upon the earth.

readings.value: And a river went out of Eden to water the garden; and from thence it was parted, and became into four heads.

verse_text.note: single source — cross-translation comparison arrives with additional verse_text sources

readings.value: The name of the first is Pison: that is it which compasseth the whole land of Havilah, where there is gold;

verse_text.note: single source — cross-translation comparison arrives with additional verse_text sources

verse_text.note: single source — cross-translation comparison arrives with additional verse_text sources

verse_text.note: single source — cross-translation comparison arrives with additional verse_text sources

readings.value: And the name of the third river is Hiddekel: that is it which goeth toward the east of Assyria. And the fourth river is Euphrates.

readings.value: And the Lord God took the man, and put him into the garden of Eden to dress it and to keep it.

verse_text.note: single source — cross-translation comparison arrives with additional verse_text sources

readings.value: And the Lord God commanded the man, saying, Of every tree of the garden thou mayest freely eat:

verse_text.note: single source — cross-translation comparison arrives with additional verse_text sources

verse_text.note: single source — cross-translation comparison arrives with additional verse_text sources

verse_text.note: single source — cross-translation comparison arrives with additional verse_text sources

verse_text.note: single source — cross-translation comparison arrives with additional verse_text sources
